final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That narrower framing is more accurate than treating rollout controls as sufficient by themselves, but it still does not satisfy the governing predicate. The policy allows rollout controls and post-launch monitoring to mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or there is reviewed risk acceptance explaining why continued exposure is acceptable. Admissible evidence shows the opposite gap remains: the affected claims subrogation review segment stays exposed in the 6% rollout, the risk acceptance is incomplete and not approved, and there is no evidence of completed pre-launch disclosure approval. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, reversibility, and public governance guidance support part of the Actor's operational story, but they do not close the missing compliance link. That makes the current certification case still suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats, because the caveat here is not merely a disclosure note attached to an otherwise satisfied policy condition; it is the unresolved condition itself.
remaining_concerns: The affected claims subrogation review segment remains eligible in the initial rollout cohort, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy condition by exclusion.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not expressly address the exposed claims subrogation review segment.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure for the named launch use case has been completed and approved before launch.
The Actor's narrowed position is still contingent on future disclosure and monitoring rather than completed evidence satisfying the pre-launch policy predicate now.
